judgements.justification: B's Reviewer_69AE rated at confidence 5 after reading 'until page 5', and B's AC presented its VAE objection as the reviewers' shared view.
B's 69AE and ATkA read the lossless-optimality framing from variational-inference and information-bottleneck positions and made it central, while A's 9TAc found it hard to digest and moved on.
A's meta-review argued only that all reviewers wanted acceptance and gave no reason for the spotlight beyond 'a strong paper'.
The paper is theoretical with one experiment; neither committee checked baselines against published results, and the Dai and Wipf dispute concerned a missing comparison section, not baseline scores.
B's AC wrote that the reviewers 'were not convinced' on VAE applicability although only 69AE held that view and ATkA wrote 'In contrast to reviewer 69AE', in the direction of rejection.
Neither committee raised breadth of audience or another venue.
B had a misreading detractor (69AE), but B's chair rejected rather than arguing acceptance against that score.
Neither forum received new experiments; both committees got promised text changes only.
No committee had a high-confidence expert rating above lower-confidence peers; B's highest-confidence review (69AE, 5) was the lowest rating.
69AE's objections were raised in the review period and the authors answered them; its late post raised its score rather than adding an unanswerable objection.
B's lower ratings matched less favourable verbal assessments (a 'firm no', central framing objections), not a stricter scale for the same praise.
B's AC penalised overclaiming, but A did not take the claims at face value: e4Tf flagged Theorem 4's quantifiers and A's AC required more careful quantification.
B's 6s came at confidence 3 to 4 from reviewers who engaged the theory and raised scores after discussion; none said they could not check the technical core.
